text:
alex: Kicking off prod deploy for release v2.3.1 in the 16:00-17:00 PDT change window. Canary at 10% for 15m. Pin is model-serving@sha:abc123. Runbooks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-backout and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-guidance. 

deploy-bot: Deploy started — job id db-2026-03-20-88. Canary target set to 10%. Notifying oncall. :rocket:

marta: noted. quick reminder: KMS rotation will be tested tomorrow in staging, so double-check key id kw-44 is being used by the private deploys (not this hosted flow).

chris: For rollback triggers — follow runbook section "Immediate Abort". TL;DR: if error_rate > 2% sustained for 3m OR p95 latency > 500ms for 5m, abort canary and unpin. Backout pin target: model-serving@sha:abc122 (previous stable).

chris: Rollback command (ops creds required):
```bash
# mark release as aborted and pin previous image
./releasectl abort --job db-2026-03-20-88 --reason "canary-failure"
./releasectl pin --service model-serving --sha abc122
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/model-serving
```

ops-oncall: I'll be primary for the window, reachable on pager. I have permission to run releasectl and to perform the unpin. If chris or alex call abort, I'll execute and post timestamps.

deploy-bot: Canary health check: p50 120ms, p95 380ms, error_rate 0.3% — all green. :white_check_mark:

tina: Smoke tests passing for API surface. I'll keep a simple test running against the canary every 2m (login, inference, embedding). If any smoke fails, I'll flag it here immediately.

alex: Decision matrix we've agreed: immediate abort on chris thresholds OR manual abort if we see functional regression in smoke tests. If abort happens, we will: 1) scale canary to 0% 2) pin previous sha 3) notify customers via release-notes channel and update status page.

marta: Minor ask — update runbook to include the releasectl abort output check. I ran into a case last week where abort returned 202 with a delayed pin. Need clearer guidance on expected timing and how to validate.

release-coordinator: Good point. Add to follow-up: add expected timeline (abort -> pin -> rollout restart within 2 minutes) and a checklist to verify imageSHA on pods.

alex: One more: change-window ops — if we hit an abort inside the first 5m of canary, we prefer immediate unpin. If later (after 15m) we can consider hotfix branch only with sign-off from eng leads.

chris: Also adding a short emergency comms template to the runbook for customers/sales to paste into customer channels. Helps speed up external messaging.

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: post-deploy checklist will run at +20m to verify rollout completion and adjust metrics retention.

ops-oncall: I'll create a short shortcut in the runbook for the exact commands and who to call (pager and 3 backups).

release-coordinator: After the deploy, please file a quick deploy notes entry: what thresholds we used, any manual aborts, and whether the pin succeeded. If we had to abort, include logs of releasectl abort and kubectl get pods output.

alex: Ok team — proceeding. If anyone sees anything odd ping here first. We'll reconvene in 30m in case of anomalies. :thumbsup:
